name: finance_timeseries
title: Time Series (all assets on one axis)
description: Universal data spine: OHLCV time series for every asset class on ONE shared time axis (stocks, FRED macro, futures, crypto, and prediction-market odds), with per-series return and annualized-volatility stats. PRESETS ARE THE POWER FEATURE — the `preset` arg pulls a whole curated domain in ONE call (18 available) and composes with ad-hoc `tickers` in the same call (e.g. preset=macro + tickers=NVDA,SMH gives the macro backdrop plus your names). Key presets: `macro` (34 series — CPI/PCE/jobs/GDP/rates/debt/M2 + live oil/gold/BTC), `recession` (Sahm rule, 10Y-2Y & 10Y-3M, claims, Chicago Fed), `credit` (full ICE BofA OAS stack IG→BBB→HY→BB→B→CCC→EM), `financial_conditions` (NFCI/STLFSI/VIX), `inflation`, `labor`, `housing`, `yield_curve` (1mo–30Y), `real_rates` (TIPS+breakevens), `consumer_credit`, `fed_balance_sheet` (QE/QT plumbing), `liquidity`, `forex_majors`, `crypto`, `sovereigns` (global 2/10/30Y yields: US, Bund, OAT, BTP, Gilt, JGB…), plus IBKR futures baskets `energy`/`commodities`/`treasuries` (full list + aliases in the `preset` arg). Reach for a preset before hand-listing tickers. For ad-hoc tickers, 18 providers auto-detect by pattern: stocks/ETFs/futures→Yahoo, FRED→FRED (or FRED: prefix), IBKR:→Interactive Brokers 15-min-delayed futures/FX/equities (e.g. IBKR:FUT:CL:NYMEX, IBKR:CASH:EUR:IDEALPRO), CLEV:→Cleveland Fed inflation nowcast, KX* or Kalshi market tickers→Kalshi, numeric 6+digit→Polymarket, PYTH:→24/7 oracle, BN:→Binance spot candles with volume (BN:BTCUSDT, BN:ETHBTC, BN:BTC-FDUSD come from the global exchange, source "binance"; plain-USD pairs such as BN:BTCUSD come from Binance.US, source "binance.us", a thin venue where many bars have no trade; a bare base BN:BTC means BTCUSDT on the global exchange; series.source and upstream_id name the venue and symbol served), GOVT:→global sovereign bond YIELDS in % (CNBC; e.g. GOVT:US10Y, GOVT:FR10Y, GOVT:DE2Y, GOVT:JP30Y, GOVT:GB10Y, GOVT:IT10Y; country code + tenor; daily back to 2000, intraday 1m/5m/30m/1h ~1y; the cross-country spread and curve shape behind US Treasury term premium). PLUMBING/CREDIT/LEVERAGE prefixes (no key): NAV:/PNAV:<TICKER>→SEC XBRL fund NAV/share and price÷NAV (PNAV:OBDC; NAV stamped at FILED date, never period end); BOND:<CUSIP|FINRA symbol>[:PX|:YLD]→FINRA TRACE single-bond price (% par) or yield % (BOND:21873SAG3:YLD; ≥1d = end-of-day print, <1d = trade candles ~1y; find CUSIPs with finance_bonds); BUYBACK:<bucket>[:OFFERED|ACCEPTED|MAX|COVER|FILL|ISSUES]→Treasury buyback ops (BUYBACK:20-30Y:COVER; one point per operation, stamped at op close); NYFED:<series>→SRF/RRP ops + SOFR/EFFR/BGCR/TGCR, _P1.._P99 percentiles, _VOL (NYFED:SRF, NYFED:SOFR_P99; rates stamped at next-day PUBLICATION, so FRED dates differ by a day); OFR:<mnemonic>→OFR repo/hedge-fund monitors + Financial Stress Index (OFR:FSI, OFR:REPO-DVP_OV_TOT-P; stamped at OBSERVATION date though released T+1 or later: no same-day causality); ETF:<TICKER>[:SO|NAV|AUM|FLOW|FLOW5|FLOW20]→shares outstanding / creations-redemptions in $mn (ETF:JNK:FLOW, ETF:SPY:FLOW; SSGA+ProShares full history, iShares/Direxion snapshot only); CBOE:→VX futures (CBOE:VX1, CBOE:VX2-VX1, CBOE:VXCONTANGO), daily put/call (CBOE:PCR_EQUITY, CBOE:PCR_SPX), chain snapshots CBOE:<GEX|ZEROGAMMA|PCR_OI|0DTE_SHARE|IV30|SPOT>:<ROOT> (CBOE:GEX:SPX); HL:<COIN>[:PX|FUNDING|FUNDING_APR|PREMIUM|OI|OI_USD]→Hyperliquid perps (HL:BTC:FUNDING_APR); DERIBIT:<DVOL|FUNDING|FUNDING_APR|SKEW25>:<ARG>→Deribit (DERIBIT:DVOL:BTC, DERIBIT:SKEW25:BTC:30D). ETF: and CBOE: are DAILY whatever the granularity (flows summed, never resampled). LIVE-ONLY single point at fetch time, no history (errors when as_of is >1h in the past; build history by polling): CBOE chain snapshots, HL OI/OI_USD, DERIBIT SKEW25. `sources` lists providers returned; every candle has a 't' timestamp — check it for freshness. OUTPUT NOTES: candles omit o/h/l when o==h==l==c AND no volume printed — for macro point series, carried-forward buckets in thin prediction markets, and the zero-volume bucket at a session boundary (a {t,c,v:0} candle at 20:00Z means the equity session ENDED there, not that price was flat). US equity INTRADAY series include pre/post-market bars; analytics.stats carries last + last_at — compare last_at to generated_at to judge staleness, and omit v when the whole series has zero volume (indices). Exchange candles (BN:) always carry v: a bar with no trade is {t,c,v:0} with the last price carried, a traded bar has v>0. `sources` lists every provider actually present; top-level `provider` is only the dispatch bucket. status: absent=all ok, partial=some tickers failed (see errors[]), error=nothing returned. Prediction-market ids come from finance_odds markets[].ticker (a bare Polymarket slug does not resolve; a Kalshi event ticker and POLYMARKET:EVENT:<event_ticker> return their legs, up to 30 deepest, and Polymarket adds an event_legs notice naming each leg). Polymarket: <id> is the Yes path, <id>:NO the No token's own path; candles come from observed prices (o/h/l/c = first/max/min/last in the bucket, stamped at bucket START, no volume; a bucket with no observation is omitted, never carried forward); 1m and 5m are true resolution and history reaches back over a year; when only coarser data exists a granularity_downgrade notice says so; a settled market ends at its payout (1 or 0). Kalshi serves every granularity: 1m native, 5m/15m/30m resampled from 1m bars with Kalshi's hourly semantics (o/h/l/c from TRADES in the bucket, v = contracts summed; a bucket with no trade shows the yes bid/ask mid; a minute with no activity carries the last close forward with v:0), candles stamped at bucket START; native 1h/1d bars are stamped at bar END. Every Kalshi markets[].ticker joins as-is, KX or not (CONTROLS-2026-D); only a one-dash non-KX event ticker needs KALSHI: (KALSHI:CONTROLS-2026). Kalshi markets settled before its historical cutoff come from Kalshi's archive automatically, so past FOMC or election legs return their pre-settlement path.

preset.description: Pass preset=list to get the full catalog with each preset's exact tickers; preset=<name> pulls the basket and composes with `tickers` in the same call (e.g. preset=macro + tickers=NVDA,SMH). 20 presets: macro, yield_curve, sovereigns (US/DE/FR 2-10-30Y, IT/ES/UK/JP/CA/AU/CH/CN via GOVT:), stress_plumbing (BDC PNAV, CoreWeave/Oracle bond yields, buyback cover, SRF, SOFR p99, OFR FSI + repo, JNK/SPY flows, VIX contango, put/call, BTC funding + DVOL, CCC OAS), private_credit (BDCs + CLO ETFs), liquidity, credit (ICE BofA OAS), financial_conditions (NFCI/STLFSI4/VIX), recession (Sahm/spreads/claims), fed_balance_sheet (QE/QT), housing (Case-Shiller/starts/mortgage), labor (NFP/JOLTS/wages), inflation (CPI/PCE/sticky/median), real_rates (TIPS), consumer_credit (delinquency/SLOOS), forex_majors, crypto, energy (WTI/Brent/NG/RBOB/HO/Gasoil via IBKR), commodities (CL/GC/SI/HG/grains/softs via IBKR), treasuries (ZT/ZF/ZN/ZB/VIX futures via IBKR). IBKR-backed baskets auto-fall-back to Yahoo front-month when IB Gateway is down.

tickers.description: Comma-separated. Stocks: AAPL,SPY,CL=F. FRED: UNRATE,T10Y2Y. IBKR futures: IBKR:FUT:CL:NYMEX, IBKR:FUT:GC:COMEX. IBKR FX: IBKR:CASH:EUR:IDEALPRO. IBKR equities: IBKR:STK:2222:TADAWUL. Cleveland Fed: CLEV:CPI,CLEV:COREPCE. Pyth: PYTH:OIL,PYTH:BTC. Kalshi: KXNBERRECESSQ-Q1-2026, CONTROLS-2026-D, or an event like KXFEDDECISION-26DEC (all legs). Polymarket: 609655, 609655:NO, or POLYMARKET:EVENT:<event_ticker> (all legs). Binance: BN:BTCUSDT, BN:ETHBTC, BN:BTC-FDUSD (global exchange), BN:BTCUSD (Binance.US). Sovereign yields: GOVT:US10Y,GOVT:FR10Y,GOVT:DE10Y,GOVT:JP30Y (any CC+tenor, e.g. GOVT:IT2Y). Fund NAV: NAV:OBDC, PNAV:FSK. Bonds: BOND:21873SAG3:YLD, BOND:68389XEC5:PX. Buybacks: BUYBACK:10-20Y:COVER. NY Fed: NYFED:SRF, NYFED:SOFR_P99. OFR: OFR:FSI, OFR:REPO-DVP_OV_TOT-P. ETF flows: ETF:JNK:FLOW, ETF:HYG:AUM. CBOE: CBOE:VXCONTANGO, CBOE:PCR_EQUITY, CBOE:GEX:SPX. Hyperliquid: HL:BTC:FUNDING_APR. Deribit: DERIBIT:DVOL:BTC. Mix freely in one call.

as_of.description: End timestamp for the window (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD). Pin this for reproducible cache hits and historical reconstruction. Defaults to now.

start.description: Explicit window start (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD). Must be used with end.

end.description: Explicit window end (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD). Must be used with start.

provider.description: Force a specific provider (auto|yahoo|fred|ibkr|pyth|binance|govt|secnav|bond|buyback|nyfed|ofr|etf|cboe|hyperliquid|deribit). Default auto routes by ticker prefix.

max_points_per_ticker.description: Safety cap. Errors if window×granularity would exceed this; suggests a coarser granularity.

name: finance_movers
title: Market Movers
description: Largest day movers across Yahoo Finance day-gainer/day-loser screeners or an explicit ticker list. Filter by direction, percent move, price, volume, min/max market cap, and sort by percent, market cap, dollar volume, or estimated market-cap value change. Served by Yahoo; pass provider=ibkr explicitly to price from IB Gateway instead (auto never consults IBKR). Outside regular hours the extended-hours overlay is automatic: price/change_pct are the FROZEN regular-session values, extended_price/extended_change_pct (with their own timestamp) are the live pre/post-market quote; market_state is normalized to premarket|regular|after_hours|closed.

universe.description: Candidate universe: day_movers, day_gainers, day_losers, or tickers. Default day_movers.

tickers.description: Comma-separated explicit tickers. If supplied, overrides screener discovery.

sort_by.description: Ranking metric. value_change = abs(market_cap * change_pct). Default value_change.

provider.description: Price/change provider. Auto uses IBKR when configured, otherwise Yahoo.

limit.description: Number of movers to return. Default 25.

scan_limit.description: Candidate count per Yahoo screener leg before local filtering/sorting. Default 100, max 250.

ibkr_market_data_type.description: Optional IBKR market data type: 1 live, 2 frozen, 3 delayed, 4 delayed-frozen.

include_extended_hours.description: If true, also fetch pre-market / after-hours move and surface as extended_price, extended_change_pct, extended_session. Sort metrics combine regular + extended when this is enabled.

name: finance_rate_path
title: Fed Rate Path Odds
description: Aggregated Polymarket+Kalshi probabilities per FOMC meeting (hold/cut/hike buckets). DERIVED — combines multiple prediction markets per meeting via volume-weighted average. Returns: meetings[] (per-meeting hold/cut/hike + n_markets + volume_total, dates snapped to actual FOMC decision day), year_view (cuts_distribution, eoy_rate_distribution, cut_by_meeting_distribution from cardinality markets), compound_paths[] (joint multi-meeting Pause-Pause-Pause paths). For raw individual markets use finance_odds.

name: finance_odds
title: Prediction Market Odds
description: Prediction market discovery + live pricing (Kalshi + Polymarket). Search accepts words, phrases, and exact tickers (round-tripping a ticker the tool returned works); exact word matches rank ahead of prefix expansions. Examples: 'recession', 'tariff', 'fed', 'oil', 'iran'. Returns probability_yes (0-1), volume_usd, bid/ask. JOIN CONTRACT: markets[].ticker is the id that joins finance_timeseries --tickers for probability HISTORY (Polymarket numeric id, Kalshi market leg like KXFEDDECISION-26JUL-H0 or CONTROLS-2026-D). A Kalshi event_ticker expands to its legs in finance_timeseries, and so does a Polymarket one written POLYMARKET:EVENT:<event_ticker>. events[] groups each Kalshi or Polymarket event with every leg (legs[]: ticker, outcome, p; mutually_exclusive when at most one leg pays), so a Fed decision or a strike ladder reads as one distribution. volume_usd is lifetime volume on both venues (volume_24h_usd is the last day). Rows add chg_24h_pp (the venue's own day-ago move) when it moved; status=settled rows carry result and settled_at. Polymarket combo/parlay legs carry combo=true and rank below single questions. trades=true with a Kalshi market or Polymarket id: prints (UTC time, yes price, contracts, taker side; Polymarket adds usd and a short wallet) over since/until with taker-yes vs taker-no totals. market=<Polymarket id> alone returns one market: bid/ask, lifetime and 24h volume, open interest, 1h/24h/1w/1mo moves, close or settlement, resolution rules, every sibling leg, and a timeseries map naming which ticker returns which outcome. If stdout omitted rows, a stdout_compaction block says how many; pass out for the full set.

search.description: Keyword or phrase (e.g. recession, fed, oil, hormuz, 'ohio senate') or an exact ticker. Kalshi searches its live index, so phrases and new markets work.

live.description: Fetch fresh prices from exchange APIs (default: true)

orderbook.description: Include orderbook depth in returned markets. Kalshi rows get orderbook.yes_bids / no_bids as [price, contracts], best first (Kalshi books hold bids only; a NO bid at q is a YES offer at 1-q).

depth.description: Number of book levels per side. Defaults to 5 if orderbook=true.

list_series.description: Kalshi only. List available series (top-level groupings).

provider.description: Force a specific venue. Default auto.

market.description: Specific market ticker or Polymarket numeric ID.

min_volume.description: Minimum lifetime USD volume per market.

top.description: Return top N markets after ranking. Different from `limit`: limit=API page size, top=post-rank cutoff.

sort_by.description: Sort key for local-cache search. Default relevance.

category.description: Category filter. On Polymarket it also matches event tags (e.g. elections, crypto).

profile.description: Query profile. macro narrows to Fed/CPI/etc., broad casts wider.

country.description: Country filter for local-cache search (v1: US only).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for Kalshi list endpoints.

deltas_only.description: Only return markets that changed since last sync. Requires sync delta index.

explain.description: Include compact ranking explanations in local-cache search output.

max_pages.description: Max pages to fetch from Kalshi list endpoints. Default unbounded.

min_delta_pp.description: Minimum absolute probability move (percentage points) since last sync. Requires sync delta index.

status.description: Search: open (default), closed, settled, all (both venues; settled rows carry result + settled_at). List endpoints: passed through.

closing_within.description: Search: only legs closing inside this window (30m, 6h, 2d, 1w).

trades.description: With market: recent trades. Polymarket id: taker fills with usd, filter with min_trade_usd. Kalshi ticker: tick-level prints over since/until, taker-side totals, the largest prints (limit, default 50) in time order; prints before Kalshi's archive cutoff come from the archive.

since.description: Trades window start: RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD, or a lookback like 6h, 2d (default 24h).

until.description: Trades window end: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD (default now).

min_contracts.description: Kalshi trades: only prints of at least this many contracts.

min_trade_usd.description: Polymarket trades: only prints of at least this many USD.

name: finance_options
title: Options Chain
description: Options chain with provider-native quotes/IV where available, put/call OI ratio, max pain, and vol skew. Default provider is auto: Yahoo baseline plus opportunistic IBKR delayed/model overlay when Gateway/TWS is reachable. Use provider=yahoo for Yahoo-only or provider=ibkr for IBKR-only debugging. Yahoo IV is passthrough and filtered fail-closed for placeholder values; Yahoo does not provide Greeks. Max pain filters out pre-split strike artifacts. For full chain across ALL expirations with IV term structure and OI concentration, pass all=true. Top-level `atm_iv` mirrors `metrics.atm_iv` (jq `.atm_iv`); in `all=true` mode it reflects the nearest non-expired snapshot's ATM IV.

ticker.description: Underlying ticker (e.g. SPY, NVDA, AAPL, QQQ)

provider.description: Data provider. Default auto uses Yahoo baseline and overlays IBKR delayed/model fields when Gateway/TWS is reachable. Use yahoo for Yahoo-only or ibkr for direct IBKR-only.

ibkr_account.description: Optional IBKR account override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_host.description: Optional IBKR host override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_port.description: Optional IBKR port override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_client_id.description: Optional IBKR client id override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_market_data_type.description: Optional IBKR market data type: 1 live, 2 frozen, 3 delayed, 4 delayed-frozen.

as_of.description: Optional as-of timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339). Current options providers support live/delayed snapshot chains only; historical full-chain as_of requests are rejected instead of relabeled.

all.description: Fetch ALL expirations with cross-expiry analytics: IV term structure, OI concentration, max pain range. Large output auto-saves to file.

summary.description: Return summary metrics only, no full chain (default: true)

near_money.description: Only return strikes within this % of the underlying (e.g. 5)

target_dte.description: Target days to expiry. If set without explicit expiry, picks the nearest listed expiry.

expirations.description: List available expirations only (no chain data).

expiry.description: Specific expiration date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use --expirations first to see valid dates.

type.description: Filter chain by option type. Default both.

name: finance_fundamentals
title: Company Fundamentals
description: Quarterly financial statements: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow. Not for ETFs — use finance_timeseries instead.

tickers.description: Comma-separated list of tickers, e.g. AAPL,MSFT,NVDA. Single ticker returns array of 1.

name: finance_search
title: Ticker and Series Search
description: Search for ticker symbols or FRED macro series IDs by name. Use before timeseries when you don't know the exact ticker/series ID.

query.description: Search query (e.g. tesla, unemployment, S&P 500, crude oil)

provider.description: Search provider. Default auto uses the normal Yahoo+FRED discovery path; ibkr uses IBKR contract search when Gateway/TWS is reachable.

ibkr_account.description: Optional IBKR account override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_host.description: Optional IBKR host override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_port.description: Optional IBKR port override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_client_id.description: Optional IBKR client id override when provider=ibkr.

ibkr_market_data_type.description: Optional IBKR market data type: 1 live, 2 frozen, 3 delayed, 4 delayed-frozen.

name: finance_filings
title: SEC Filings
description: SEC filings by ticker (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, ...). READ A FILING PRECISELY IN TWO CALLS, no max_chars guessing: (1) toc=true (with forms, e.g. forms='10-Q', or accession=...) returns the latest filing's table of contents: every section's id, title and exact size in characters — 10-K/10-Q items (risk factors, MD&A, controls, legal proceedings, ...), each primary financial statement (income_statement, comprehensive_income, balance_sheet, cash_flow, equity), the notes and every numbered note under its own title (note:5 = 'Note 5. Inventories'), the auditor's report, 8-K items, and exhibits such as ex99.1 (the earnings press release), with the statements inside an earnings release listed under it (ex99.1:income_statement, ex99.1:balance_sheet, ex99.1:cash_flow, plus titled tables such as segment results). (2) section=<ids> returns exactly that clean text and nothing else (tables as aligned plain-text rows with | between columns, page numbers and TOC noise removed); comma-separate several: section='cash_flow,note:inventories,mda'. On an earnings 8-K, section=cash_flow returns the cash flow table from the press release (or name it: ex99.1:cash_flow). Aliases: mda, risk_factors, business, legal_proceedings, notes (all notes, where the unusual items hide), note:<number or words>, press_release, document (everything). NUMBERS AS DATA: xbrl=true returns the filing's XBRL facts as JSON (concept, label, value, unit, period, and the section id the number sits in, so you can pull the prose behind it) with prior-quarter (qoq), year-ago (yoy) and prior fiscal-year-end (vs_fye) values and % changes; default = every line of the primary statements plus facts elsewhere that moved >= 25% (~30-50k chars); xbrl_concepts='Inventory,Revenue' returns just those concepts, every period. On an earnings 8-K (no XBRL until the 10-Q), xbrl=true returns the press release's tables in the same shape: values exactly as printed, period from the column headers, unit from the caption, concept 'release:<label>' (never mapped to us-gaap), yoy / vs_fye from the release's own columns and qoq from the previous earnings release. WHAT CHANGED: section=risk_factors,mda with diff=true compares each section with the same section of the previous filing of that form and returns only the differences, as exact text: added and removed paragraphs, the added and removed sentences of changed paragraphs (located by their opening words and subheading), and counts of paragraphs that differ only in numbers, dates and period words (figures_only, not printed), moved and unchanged. A 10-Q's risk factors are compared with the 10-K when the 10-K is newer than the previous 10-Q, or when the 10-Q only lists updates to it (then 10-K paragraphs it does not restate are counted, not listed). diff_against=<accession> picks the earlier filing. Tables are not compared (xbrl does numbers). toc/section/xbrl read one filing (limit 1) unless limit is set. Without these flags: metadata and SEC URLs (over this connector also raw_text, the first 50k chars of the document). search_text (no ticker) = market-wide full-text search: 'which companies filed 8-Ks mentioning X this week'.

limit.description: Max filings (default 5; 1 when toc/section/xbrl is set)

accession.description: Read one specific filing by accession number (e.g. 0000320193-26-000024, dashes optional). Overrides forms/limit.

toc.description: Table of contents of the filing: every section's id, title, kind (item/statement/notes/note/report/exhibit/subsection), level and size in chars (what section=<id> will return). On an 8-K / 6-K the statements and titled tables inside the earnings release appear under their exhibit (ex99.1:cash_flow). Cheap first call, a few thousand chars.

section.description: Comma-separated TOC ids or aliases; returns exactly those sections' clean text, whole (no cap unless max_chars). Examples: 'cash_flow', 'balance_sheet,income_statement', 'note:inventories', 'note:7', 'notes', 'mda', 'risk_factors', 'part2_item1a', 'item7', 'item2.02', 'ex99.1', 'ex99.1:balance_sheet', 'press_release', 'document'. On an 8-K, statement aliases reach the statements inside the earnings release.

xbrl.description: Return the filing's inline-XBRL facts with comparisons: each row has concept, label (the filing's own row label), section (TOC id where it appears), dims (segment etc.), period ('3M ended 2026-09-30', 'at 2026-09-30'), unit ('USD millions'), value as printed, and qoq / yoy / vs_fye {period, value, change, pct, from}. Default selection: primary statement line items + facts elsewhere that moved >= xbrl_min_change %. On an earnings 8-K / 6-K: the press release's tables in this shape (source 'press release EX-99.1 tables', values as printed, concept 'release:<label>'), before the 10-Q XBRL exists.

xbrl_concepts.description: Comma-separated, case-insensitive substrings of XBRL concept names or row labels (e.g. 'Inventory', 'RevenueFromContract,Goodwill'; on an earnings 8-K, the release's row labels); returns every matching fact in the filing, all periods/dimensions, with comparisons. '*' = every current-period fact (large). Implies xbrl=true.

xbrl_min_change.description: Percent change that flags a fact outside the primary statements as a mover (default 25); on an earnings 8-K, a row of the release's other tables (segments, products).

diff.description: With section: return what changed in each section against the same section of the previous filing of the same form, instead of its text. sections[].diff = {base {form, filing_date, accession_number, section_id}, note, added[] {under, text}, removed[] {under, text}, changed[] {under, at, added_sentences, removed_sentences}, figures_only, figures_only_under, moved, unchanged, not_restated, paragraphs, chars}. Every string is exact filing text. Call again without diff for the full text.

diff_against.description: Accession of the earlier filing to compare against (implies diff), e.g. the previous 10-Q when the default picked the 10-K.

download.description: Download primary filing documents and index JSON to local cache. Default: true

single_file.description: Download exactly one file: the primary document for the most recent matching filing. Forces limit=1 and skips index/exhibits. Default: false

download_all.description: Download every file listed in each filing index, including exhibits/attachments. Default: false

important_exhibits.description: Download filtered useful text exhibits such as EX-99, earnings releases, and slides while skipping image/XBRL/support noise. Default: true unless download=false

include_text.description: Deprecated alias for download=true; no text parsing or inline excerpt is performed

raw_text.description: Include the whole primary document as clean text inline (tables aligned, page furniture removed). Prefer toc + section to get exactly the part you need; use max_chars to cap this.

max_chars.description: Cap for raw_text / press_release_text, and for each section when given. Sections come back whole by default: read their sizes from toc instead of guessing a cap.

user_agent.description: Optional SEC User-Agent override with contact email, e.g. eli-cli (mailto:me@example.com)

search_text.description: Cross-filer FULL-TEXT search: return filings from ANY company whose documents contain this phrase (e.g. "share repurchase", "data center", "going concern"). ticker not required in this mode; combine with forms/from/to to scope. Same-day EDGAR freshness.

from.description: Earliest filing date for search_text mode (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Latest filing date for search_text mode (YYYY-MM-DD).

press_release_text.description: For earnings 8-Ks (item 2.02): inline the press-release exhibit as parsed plain text instead of the XBRL cover doc.

name: finance_schedule
title: Earnings and Macro Calendar
description: Earnings calendar (Nasdaq) + macro release calendar (FRED). Shows upcoming CPI, PCE, GDP, jobs, FOMC, claims, and earnings dates. Use min_cap (e.g. '50B') to filter large-cap earnings only.

major.description: Macro: keep just major US releases

macro_profile.description: Macro filtering profile. broad=all releases, market=common-watched only, major=top-tier only. The boolean `major` is a shortcut for macro_profile=major.

name: finance_auctions
title: Treasury Auctions
description: Recent US Treasury auction results: bid-to-cover, direct/indirect bidder pct, high yield, total accepted, total tendered, CUSIP, security type, security term, auction/issue/maturity dates.

security_type.description: all, bill, note, bond, tips, frn (default: all)

name: finance_cot
title: CFTC Commitments of Traders
description: CFTC Commitment of Traders weekly positions (specs vs commercials, longs/shorts/net, OI, week-over-week change). Released Friday for prior Tuesday. Natural query matching — use 'crude', 'gold', '10-year', 'spx', 'yen', 'treasury'. Auto-detects financial vs disaggregated report. Includes historical percentile rank across the requested window.

query.description: Natural query: gold, crude, 10-year, spx, treasury, yen, bitcoin

report.description: disaggregated (commodities) or financial (rates/FX/equity). Auto-detected if omitted

limit.description: Max distinct contracts to return (default: 15). Use higher for broad queries

name: finance_nyfed
title: NY Fed Rates and Operations
description: NY Fed Markets data: overnight reference rates (SOFR, EFFR, OBFR, TGCR, BGCR with percentiles and volume), ON RRP facility (total amount, counterparties, rate), SOMA holdings (Fed balance sheet by security type), primary dealer positions. Real-time Fed plumbing data.

kind.description: rates (SOFR/EFFR/OBFR/TGCR/BGCR), rrp (reverse repo facility), soma (Fed balance sheet), dealers (primary dealer positions). Default: rates

name: finance_volsurface
title: CBOE Volatility Indices
description: CBOE volatility indices: VIX (30-day), VIX9D (9-day), VIX3M (3-month), VIX6M (6-month), VIX1Y (1-year), VVIX (vol-of-vol), OVX (oil), GVZ (gold), SKEW. Returns latest OHLC + optional history. Not a per-underlying strike/expiry implied-vol surface.

history.description: Trading days of history (default: latest only)

name: finance_stress
title: OFR Financial Stress Index
description: OFR Financial Stress Index (composite + credit/equity/funding/safe-assets/volatility components). Daily, updated T+1. Index is z-scored vs OFR's own historical baseline; raw values returned without categorical labeling.

name: finance_bonds
title: Corporate Bonds (FINRA TRACE)
description: FINRA TRACE corporate/agency bond lookup: an issuer's outstanding bonds (CUSIP, FINRA symbol, coupon %, maturity, last sale price + yield, last trade date), sorted by maturity. FINRA matches the EXACT issuer name only (e.g. "ORACLE CORP", "COREWEAVE INC", "META PLATFORMS INC"; "META" returns nothing). Not a timeseries: feed a returned cusip into finance_timeseries as BOND:<CUSIP>:YLD (yield %) or BOND:<CUSIP>:PX (price, % of par).

issuer.description: Exact FINRA issuer name, case-insensitive (e.g. ORACLE CORP).

cusip.description: Look up one bond by 9-char CUSIP or FINRA issue symbol (e.g. 21873SAG3, CRWV6364372). Overrides issuer.

name: finance_fiscal
title: US Fiscal Data
description: Treasury fiscal data: daily national debt total (public + intragovernmental, in billions), daily Treasury operating cash balance (deposits/withdrawals), average interest rates by security type.

kind.description: debt (daily national debt), statement (Treasury cash balance), interest (avg rates by security). Default: debt

name: finance_ecb
title: European Central Bank Data
description: ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (SDMX): EUR exchange rates, Euro STR, M3 money supply, EURIBOR term structure, euro area yield curve, Eurosystem balance sheet. No auth required. Presets or custom SDMX dataset+key.

preset.description: eurusd | fx_majors (USD/GBP/JPY/CHF/CNY) | estr (Euro Short-Term Rate) | m3 (money supply) | euribor (1M/3M/6M/12M term structure) | yield_curve (3M-30Y spot rates) | balance_sheet (Eurosystem total assets)

dataset.description: SDMX dataset ID (EXR, FM, EST, BSI, YC). Use with key.

key.description: SDMX dimension key (e.g. D.USD.EUR.SP00.A). Use with dataset.

start.description: Start period YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM. Default: 2025-01-01

end.description: End period (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM). Defaults to now.

name: finance_eia
title: EIA Energy Data
description: EIA (U.S. Energy Information Administration): weekly petroleum inventories (crude oil, gasoline, distillate stocks) and natural gas storage. Preset-driven: crude | gasoline | distillate | all | nat_gas (or a custom `route`). Requires EIA_API_KEY env var (free registration at eia.gov/opendata).

preset.description: crude (US crude oil stocks excl SPR) | gasoline | distillate | all (crude+gasoline+distillate+Cushing) | nat_gas (Lower 48 working storage)

route.description: Custom EIA API route (e.g. petroleum/stoc/wstk/data/). Overrides preset.

name: finance_bis
title: BIS Central Bank Data
description: BIS (Bank for International Settlements): global central bank policy rates, total assets, credit-to-GDP gaps, property prices, real effective exchange rates. Covers 40-50 economies. Preset-driven: policy_rates | assets | credit_gap | property | eer (or a custom SDMX dataset+key). No auth.

preset.description: policy_rates (US/EU/JP/GB/CH/CN) | assets (CB total assets in local ccy) | credit_gap (credit-to-GDP gap) | property (real residential prices) | eer (real effective exchange rates)

countries.description: Comma-separated ISO codes: US,XM(Euro area),JP,GB,CH,CN,AU,CA. Default: US,XM,JP,GB

dataset.description: BIS SDMX dataset (e.g. WS_CBPOL). Use with `key` for direct query, bypassing presets.

key.description: SDMX dimension key (e.g. M.US+XM+JP+GB). Use with `dataset`.

name: finance_boj
title: Bank of Japan Data
description: Bank of Japan: monetary base, BOJ balance sheet (total assets, JGB holdings, ETF holdings), TANKAN business sentiment DI, call rate, M2/M3 money stock, USD/JPY. Preset-driven: policy_rate | call_rate | monetary_base | balance_sheet | money_stock | tankan | fx (or custom db+codes). New Feb 2026 API, no auth.

preset.description: policy_rate | call_rate | monetary_base | balance_sheet | money_stock (M2+M3) | tankan (Mfg+Non-Mfg large DI) | fx (USD/JPY)

db.description: BOJ database name (e.g. IR01, FM01, BS01, CO). Use with codes for direct query.

name: finance_boe
title: Bank of England Data
description: Bank of England: Bank Rate, SONIA, gilt yields (5Y/10Y/20Y par and zero-coupon), M4 money supply, GBP exchange rates. Preset-driven: bank_rate | sonia | gilts | m4 | fx | all (or custom `codes`). CSV endpoint, no auth.

preset.description: bank_rate | sonia | gilts (5Y/10Y/20Y yields) | m4 (money supply) | fx (GBP/USD, GBP/EUR, GBP/JPY) | all (dashboard: rate+SONIA+10Y+M4+GBPUSD)

codes.description: Comma-separated BOE series codes (e.g. IUDBEDR,IUDSOIA,IUDMNPY). Use instead of preset for custom queries.

end.description: End date DD/Mon/YYYY format like 01/Jan/2026, or 'now'. Defaults to now.

name: finance_curve
title: Futures Forward Curve
description: Futures forward curve for commodities. Returns every contract month's price, front month price, back month price, raw spread (back-front), and spread_pct. Supported: oil/wti, brent, gold, silver, natgas, copper, platinum, palladium, gasoline/rbob, heating/ho.

commodity.description: Commodity to chart: oil, brent, gold, silver, natgas, copper, platinum, palladium, gasoline, heating

months.description: Number of forward months to include (default 12, max 24)

list.description: List supported commodities and exit (no curve data).

name: finance_log
title: Tool Call Log
description: Query the local activity trail: a tamper-evident (hash-chained), append-only record of every finance tool invocation, with the FULL response payload of each call archived content-addressed so the exact information basis of past research can be reconstructed and proven. Filter by time window or substring; verify chain integrity; replay any archived payload by seq; per-tool usage stats. Local files only.

tail.description: Show the last N matching entries (default 20).

grep.description: Only entries containing this substring (case-insensitive), e.g. a ticker or tool name.

since.description: Only entries at/after this ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.

stats.description: Return per-tool aggregate stats (calls, avg duration, errors) instead of raw entries.

until.description: Only entries at/before this ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.

verify.description: Verify the hash chain over the whole trail; reports the first altered/removed/reordered record.

show_payload.description: Print the exact archived response payload for a record seq, integrity-checked against its recorded hash.

name: finance_insider
title: Insider Trades (SEC Form 4)
description: Parsed insider transactions from SEC Form 4 filings for a ticker: who bought/sold, role (director/officer/10% owner), transaction code (P=purchase S=sale A=award M=exercise), shares, price, value, shares owned after — plus buy/sell summary (net shares, net value, unique insiders). T+2-business-day freshness from EDGAR.

ticker.description: Ticker to fetch insider transactions for.

summary_only.description: Only the buy/sell summary metrics, no rows.

name: finance_short
title: Short Interest (FINRA)
description: FINRA short-selling data for a ticker, two cadences in one call: consolidated short interest (bi-monthly settlement print: shares short, days-to-cover, change vs prior period) and Reg SHO daily short volume (per-venue off-exchange short-sale volume + short ratio, T+1/T+2 fresh) — the positioning/squeeze layer for equities, complementing finance_cot for futures.

name: report_issue
title: Report a Problem with Market Search
description: Report a problem with Market Search itself to its developer: a bug, wrong or stale data, a confusing result, or a missing capability. Use it when a finance_* tool errors, returns numbers you have reason to believe are wrong or out of date, behaves in a way its description does not explain, or cannot do something the user reasonably needed. Say which tool you called, the arguments, what you expected, and what came back. Never include the user's private data, portfolio, positions, account details or credentials; describe the problem in general terms instead. The note goes to the developer's inbox on tell.dev with the Market Search version, the operating system and the name of this client, and a copy is kept in the local activity trail (finance_log). The developer cannot reply through this tool. After it is sent, tell the user in one line that you reported it. Not for market questions or for contacting anyone other than the Market Search developer.

message.description: What happened: the tool called, what you expected, what came back, and why it looks wrong. Plain text, up to 8000 bytes.

kind.description: bug (default; includes wrong or stale data), idea (a missing capability), question (a confusing result or description), praise, other.

tool.description: The Market Search tool involved, e.g. finance_timeseries.

arguments.description: The arguments you passed to that tool, as JSON text. Cut to 500 bytes. Leave out anything private.

error.description: The error message, or the part of the output that looks wrong.

annotations.title: Report a Problem with Market Search
